explanation: When `ast.literal_eval` returns a string (e.g. from input like `'hello'`), the new code wraps it with `out[0]` as a quote character, returning something like `'hello'` (a string with literal quote characters) instead of the plain string `hello`, which changes the previously returned value and will break playbooks that relied on getting an unquoted string back.
